key_insight: BISECT counters spectral starvation in continual learning by splitting low-rank updates into shared invariant directions and an orthogonal novelty complement.
engineering_relevance: Although categorized as constitutive modeling, the abstract demonstrates continual visual learning rather than solid-mechanics applications, with potential relevance to updating engineering vision systems without retaining past examples.
method: Partition a fixed LoRA rank budget into dominant joint historical–current modes and a novelty complement.
Extract novelty directions using generalized Rayleigh whitening and orthogonal complement projection.
Merge trained updates into the frozen backbone, gating invariant atoms by current-to-joint Rayleigh ratios and retaining novelty atoms at unit gain.
evidence_signal: Across eight incremental settings on five vision datasets, BISECT reportedly outperforms prompt, adapter, and LoRA baselines with no extra inference parameters or FLOPs; historical null tails capture only about 5.5% of incoming-task variance.
watch_item: Training-time decomposition costs and sensitivity to rank allocation are not quantified in the abstract.
paper_title: BISECT: Bilevel Spectral Decomposition for Low-Rank Continual Learning
